text.headline:
Machine Learning
1950s - Present
text.text: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on the development of algorithms that can learn from and make predictions or decisions based on data.

text.headline: Turing Test
text.text: "I propose to consider the question, 'Can machines think?'." Because "thinking" is difficult to define, Turing chooses to "replace the question by another, which is closely related to it and is expressed in relatively unambiguous words".

media.caption: The Neural Network by Frank Rosenblatt’s Perceptron

text.headline: Neural Network
text.text: The perceptron, a simple neural network model, introduced the concept of computer learning and inspired further research in machine learning and neural networks.

text.headline: Perceptrons by Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert
text.text: In 1969, ten years after the discovery of the perceptron—which showed that a machine could be taught to perform certain tasks using examples—Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published Perceptrons, their analysis of the computational capabilities of perceptrons for specific tasks.

text.headline: Multi-layer Perceptrons
text.text: In 1986, David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams published a paper that introduced the backpropagation algorithm for training multi-layer perceptrons. This algorithm allowed neural networks to learn complex patterns and relationships in data, leading to significant advancements in machine learning.

media.caption: How convolutional neural networks were born in the late 80s

text.headline: Convolutional Neural Networks
text.text: In 1998, Yann LeCun and colleagues introduced the LeNet architecture, one of the first successful applications of convolutional neural networks for image recognition. Which stood out as a pioneering model that demonstrated the true potential of end-to-end learning for visual tasks.

text.headline: Deep Learning
text.text: In 2012, Geoffrey Hinton and colleagues introduced the AlexNet architecture, which won the ImageNet competition and sparked the deep learning boom. This marked a significant milestone in the development of neural networks for image recognition.

text.headline: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
text.text: In 2014, Ian Goodfellow and colleagues introduced the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architecture, which are models that generate new, realistic data by learning from existing data. This marked a significant milestone in the development of neural networks for image generation and other creative tasks.

text.headline: Modern Generative AI
text.text: In 2022, foundation models like GPT-3 and DALL-E have revolutionized the field of generative AI, enabling the creation of highly realistic images, text, and other forms of media. This marked a significant milestone in the development of neural networks for creative tasks.
